validation_boundary: Atoms were validated against a strict local Pydantic contract reconstructed from recent validated project LiteratureAtom artifacts and the large-source guideline guardrail. Because the governing ATOM model/schema files were not directly retrievable, this report does not claim execution of the authoritative project Pydantic/schema code.

duplicate_review.finding: No duplicate formal guidance identifiers within Recommendation and Practice Point namespaces, and all atom_id values are unique. Recommendation and Practice Point identifiers with the same number are retained as distinct source assertions.

consistency_review.finding: Recommendation strength and evidence certainty are preserved in tags; Practice Points are explicitly ungraded; underlying study results were not promoted to primary-study atoms.

schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom model used in recent project outputs has no dedicated guideline_recommendation or practice_point atom kind. Formal guideline statements are serialized as atom_kind="other" with descriptive tags, following the large-source guideline guardrail.
extraction_limitations: Canonical statements were normalized from the PDF text layer to repair line-wrap hyphenation, ligatures, inequality symbols, and fused citation markers.

The ATOM schema is oriented toward primary literature; this extraction captures the guideline’s formal assertions and methods rather than treating evidence summarized from cited studies as if KDIGO generated those primary data.
All atoms remain needs_review because extraction was performed by a language model without human source verification.
The data supplement was used for SEA evidence reconciliation and reference extraction; its individual evidence-profile rows were not converted to primary-study atoms.
